messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P2 — post-release anomaly detected: canary group (wave-7) showing +300ms p95 latency and 40% throughput drop vs baseline. Auto-alert triggered and paging on-call.
alex_m: rolled livepatch (runtime image: rdm-runtime:2026.3.17-hotpatch) at 09:15 UTC. Canary traffic 10% -> 09:21 seeing spike. I'm tagging eng-runtime.
marta_s: seeing kernel fallback logs on canary pods: `selected kernel=fallback-kernel` repeatedly. Batch sizes dropping to 1 in traces.
ryan_o: confirmed. Metrics: token throughput down ~42%, tail latency p99 up 700ms. Error rate for long prompts trending up (502/504 from sequencer). pushing logs to /var/log/rdm/runtime/canary.log.
sre_oncall: I'm on it. Eng-runtime, can someone confirm whether hotpatch touched kernel selector or batching heuristic?
eng_runtime_lead: yes, hotpatch includes kernel-selector tunables + adaptive-batching change (delta: use-prefetch=true, min_batch=2). suspect interaction with certain model shapes causing fallback.
alex_m: can we flip the feature flag to disable the new selector? /ff toggle runtime:kernel-selector:2026-hotpatch off
marta_s: disabling selector now: `/feature-flag set runtime.selector.hotpatch false` -> applied to canary namespace. monitoring.
customer-sup: two enterprise customers reported elevated latencies and occasional 504s starting ~09:23 UTC. No data breach, just degraded performance. Notifying them we're mitigating.
ryan_o: logs show `kv_cache_miss_storm` and microthrash on prefetch paths when batching tries to grow then collapses. Kernel then falls back because preferred kernel cannot handle the request shape quickly.
sre_oncall: quick mitigation options: 1) flip flag (done), 2) scale canary down to 0 and shift traffic back to stable, 3) rollback canary image. Which do we take now?
eng_runtime_lead: flip helped on some pods but not all; prefer rollback to known-good image. Preparing rollback plan. @sre_oncall coordinate with platform to drain and revert canary.
alex_m: rollback command ready: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/rdm-runtime-canary --to-revision=2026031501 -n canary` — will start at 09:30 UTC once platform confirms drain window.
sre_oncall: platform confirmed. Draining canary hosts (graceful) and shifting 10% back to stable at 09:31.
marta_s: running `kubectl rollout undo` now, watching pod events. Also bumping scheduling priority to avoid prefetch backlog during transition.
ryan_o: hooking a temporary token-level rate-limit to long-running prompts to protect sequencer while rollback proceeds: `rlimit set sequencer.long_prompts 5rpm`.
customer-sup: sent interim status to impacted customers: "We've identified a post-release regression affecting some canary nodes. We're rolling back the canary and expect service restoration within ~10min. We'll follow up once stable." :white_check_mark:
eng_runtime_lead: rollback finished at 09:34 UTC. Canary image now rdm-runtime:2026.03.15-stable. Observability: p95 back down toward baseline, throughput recovering.
marta_s: kernel selector no longer hitting fallback in new pods. Batch sizes normalize to configured distribution. KV miss rate dropping.
ryan_o: error rate retracing downward; sequencer 504s near zero. Keep the rate-limit for another 5min then remove.
sre_oncall: on-call handoff: I'm staying on to monitor for 30m, then will hand to next oncall at 10:05 if stable. Please file an incident report and RCA ticket.
alex_m: filing RFC and short postmortem now. Root cause hypothesis: hotpatch's adaptive-batching heuristic interacted poorly with model shapes leading to kv cache patterns that forced kernel-selector to fallback, amplifying latency. Action items: revert selector change from hotpatch, add canary traffic shape tests, tighten pre-release perf gating.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status: mitigated -> rollback completed. Impact: transient latency/throughput degradation for a subset of canary traffic and two enterprise customers. Next: postmortem and follow-ups.
eng_runtime_lead: thanks all. Good triage, quick rollback. Follow-up owners: eng-runtime (kernel selector revert + tests), platform (drain automation improvements), devex (customer runbook update). :thumbsup:
